description: A one-time code input; each digit springs into its own slot, an error empties the slots from last to first, and success draws a curtain with a tick rising in the middle.
interactionNotes: Click the row and type digits; each digit springs into the next slot. You can also paste the whole code at once — the digits settle in a cascade. When the last slot fills, `onComplete` is called and whatever decision you made about the code plays out: acceptance opens an accent curtain from the middle with a tick rising, rejection empties the slots from last to first and then clears the code. The component does not decide whether the code is correct — that is your job.

props.value: The controlled code. A digit arriving from outside settles in with a cascade, and a digit that leaves empties its slot.
props.defaultValue: Initial uncontrolled code; it renders already settled from the start.
props.onChange: Called on every edit — including clearing at the end of a rejection.
props.onComplete: Once, when the last slot fills.
props.status: Error empties the slots from last to first under a danger tint and clears the code; success merges the fills into a curtain and locks the input.
props.mask: Shows a dot in place of each digit.
props.caret: Blinking caret in the active slot.
props.disabled: Dims the row and ignores input.
props.accentColor: Fill of a settled digit, the ring of the active slot, and the success curtain.
props.inkColor: The caret, and the tint of the active slot.
props.digitColor: Color of the digit on the fill.
props.dangerColor: Ring and fill color in the error state.
props.slotSize: Slot width, px. Height and digit size follow it too.
props.radius: Corner rounding, px; capped at half the slot size.
props.bounce: Spring bounce of settling; zero means damped with no bounce.
props.settle: Seconds a digit takes to settle or empty.
props.rise: Pixels a digit rises from below; zero means it only fades.
props.cascade: Milliseconds between slots when several settle together or empty in a rejection.

tips: This component does not decide whether the code is correct — you know where the right code lives. Take `onComplete` and set `status` after the server responds.
Pasting works: copy the whole code and paste it onto the row, and the digits settle in a cascade. The SMS keyboard autofill (`autocomplete="one-time-code"`) is wired up too.
Persian input is accepted too — both Persian and Arabic-Indic digit forms convert to the same Latin code. The `value` and `onChange` values are always Latin, because that is data, not display.
Filled slots are distinguishable from empty ones but **cannot be skipped**: clicking any slot moves the caret to the first empty slot and no further.
Set `cascade` to zero so all digits settle at once; raise it to make the stepped line more obvious. Above 40ms it feels slow on a six-digit code.

This component **does not mirror for right-to-left**, and that is intentional: its geometry is physical (the caret moves via `translateX` and a tap is mapped to a slot via `clientX`). Only the text and digits are Persian — the same rule as `jelly-radio`.

To let the user know you rejected a wrong code, set `status` to `error` and **then yourself** return it to `idle` once the emptying finishes — at the end the component fires `onChange('')`, which is the signal that it is done.
